hints: Focus on the carbon skeleton first, does each starting material already have the same 3-carbon chain as propanoic acid?
Recall that a primary alcohol can be oxidised in two stages to a carboxylic acid, and an aldehyde needs just one oxidation step.
Remember what happens when a nitrile is heated with aqueous acid, think about what functional group the $-C\equiv N$ carbon becomes.
walkthrough:
**Check the carbon count**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. It has 3 carbons.

All three starting materials also have 3 carbons, so no chain building or breaking is needed, only functional group change.

**Test 1, propan-1-ol**

A primary alcohol is oxidised first to an aldehyde, then to a carboxylic acid with strong oxidising agent like acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ heated under reflux.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
So 1 works.

**Test 2, propanal**

An aldehyde is already one oxidation step away from the acid. Mild oxidation completes the job.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
So 2 works.

**Test 3, propanenitrile**

Acid hydrolysis of a nitrile gives a carboxylic acid and an ammonium ion. The nitrile carbon becomes the carboxyl carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
So 3 works.

**Combine the conclusion**

Since 1, 2 and 3 can all give propanoic acid, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three routes are valid. 1 by strong oxidation of a primary alcohol, 2 by oxidation of an aldehyde, and 3 by acid hydrolysis of a nitrile. All preserve the 3-carbon skeleton.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out the nitrile. Students sometimes forget that $\text{R-CN}$ hydrolysed in dilute HCl gives $\text{R-COOH}$.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out the alcohol. Students sometimes think propan-1-ol stops at propanal, forgetting that heating under reflux with excess oxidant gives the acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. It wrongly leaves out two valid routes. Both aldehyde oxidation and nitrile hydrolysis are standard laboratory preparations of carboxylic acids.
